memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You are to lay your hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted on your behalf to make atonement for you.'" - Lev 1:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the most important sentences in the whole book. The worshipper places his hand on the animal's head — not a light touch, but a firm pressing. In that gesture he is saying: this one stands in my place. What should happen to me is happening to it.

And then comes the astonishing phrase: it will be accepted on your behalf to make atonement for you. Atonement means covering. The sinner walks away alive because something else did not.

Some people find this offensive — why should an innocent creature die for a guilty person? But that discomfort is exactly the point. Sin is not a small administrative matter that God can wave away. It costs a life. Every time an Israelite laid his hand on that head, he was being taught the weight of his own wrongdoing.

And every one of those thousands of hands was pointing forward. John the Baptist saw Jesus and said, "Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" (Jn 1:29). At the cross, God laid on Him the iniquity of us all (Isa 53:6). Christ became sin for us so that we might become the righteousness of God (2 Cor 5:21).

Lay your hand on Him by faith. He is accepted, and in Him, so are you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I take my own sin as seriously as God does?
2. Have I personally placed my trust in Christ as my substitute, or only admired Him from a distance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You took my place when I could not stand in it myself. I rest my whole hope on You, my Lamb and my atonement. Amen.
